commenti.body: I'm a bit annoyed that most streaming service mostly/only doing serials. I would be fine with a miniseries, but with the long time between season and the cancellation possibilities its hard to get invested in them.

Any book recommendations of the history of cinema (globally)? I know of the existence of things like Pre-Code Hollywood and Indian Parallel Cinema movement , but I would love to know much more: which themes were relevant, technical capabilities at the time,  an overall timeline, etc. thanks!

Lisa Odham Stokes & Michael Hoover’s City on Fire: Hong Kong Cinema has afforded endless enlightenment over the last few years. Come for thoughtful analyses of whatever Wong Kar-wai you like, stay for inside-baseball exploration of themes across decades of pre-Holdover cinema. I’ve discovered so many new favorites from this one book— Ann Hui, Peter Chan, Stanley Kwan, Clara Law, it’s crazy.

Taiwan Cinema: A Contested Nation Onscreen, by Gou-Juin Hong, likewise, goes deep on the history of Taiwanese cinema. It reads more academically, but I was hungry for some insight on Hou Hsiao-Hsien’s craft and was not disappointed. Although the availability of a lot of the earlier pictures it discusses is lacking, it’s still fascinating to learn about pioneer film movements in other parts of the world beside America.

If you want to learn more about the early days of silent filmmaking in America, though, Kevin Brownlow’s The Parade’s Gone By is the holy gospel. I didn’t know much going in, but the dissection of craft, interviews, and sort of conjuring up of the feeling of the early days of silent film— that sense of discovery and grand design and uncharted terrain— it’s like a magic trick.

If anyone can recommend anything on the history of German cinema, I’d be much indebted.
Was surprised at the amount of handheld and shakycam in The Killer, even if most of it was probably done in post. Seems like a bit of a stylistic departure for Fincher.

Thank you man! I suppose it definitely is optimistic to find all the countries in one book, so I appreciate the specificity by region. Do you have one that goes past silent era? e.g. Pre-Code till more recently

I haven’t read as much writing on that era of Hollywood— but flipping through Andrew Sarris’ The American Cinema: Directors and Direction 1929-1968, I would say, is worth your time. Beyond that, I’m not of much help, I’m afraid.
No worries. I hope to check out all of them!
